content.title: Common countability and quantifier errors
content.instructions: Each sentence contains ONE error with a countable or uncountable noun, a plural form or a quantifier. Rewrite the whole sentence correctly.

items.prompt: The internet gives students access to a vast amount of informations.
accepted_answers: The internet gives students access to a vast amount of information.
items.model_answer: The internet gives students access to a vast amount of information.
items.explanation: 'Information' is uncountable, so it never takes a plural -s. 'A vast amount of' is correct because it is used with uncountable nouns.

items.prompt: Scientists have carried out many researches into the effects of social media on sleep.
accepted_answers: Scientists have carried out a great deal of research into the effects of social media on sleep.
Scientists have carried out a lot of research into the effects of social media on sleep.
Scientists have carried out extensive research into the effects of social media on sleep.
Scientists have carried out many studies into the effects of social media on sleep.
items.model_answer: Scientists have carried out a great deal of research into the effects of social media on sleep.
items.explanation: 'Research' is uncountable, so it cannot be plural or follow 'many'. Use an uncountable quantifier (a great deal of, a lot of, extensive) or switch to a countable noun such as 'studies'.

items.prompt: In 2020, less people used public transport than in any previous year.
accepted_answers: In 2020, fewer people used public transport than in any previous year.
items.model_answer: In 2020, fewer people used public transport than in any previous year.
items.explanation: 'People' is a plural countable noun, so the comparative quantifier is 'fewer'. 'Less' is for uncountable nouns (less traffic, less time).

items.prompt: A large amount of students now choose to study abroad for their degree.
accepted_answers: A large number of students now choose to study abroad for their degree.
items.model_answer: A large number of students now choose to study abroad for their degree.
items.explanation: 'Students' is plural countable, so use 'a large number of' (with a plural verb). 'A large amount of' is for uncountable nouns: a large amount of money.

items.prompt: Parents often give their children advices about choosing a career.
accepted_answers: Parents often give their children advice about choosing a career.
items.model_answer: Parents often give their children advice about choosing a career.
items.explanation: 'Advice' is uncountable: no plural -s and no 'an'. To count it, say 'a piece of advice' or 'some advice'. (The verb 'advise' is spelt with an s.)

items.prompt: Many peoples believe that the government should ban junk food advertising.
accepted_answers: Many people believe that the government should ban junk food advertising.
items.model_answer: Many people believe that the government should ban junk food advertising.
items.explanation: 'People' is already the plural of 'person'. 'Peoples' exists only in the sense of nations or ethnic groups (the indigenous peoples of South America).

items.prompt: The amount of cars on the roads has doubled since 1990.
accepted_answers: The number of cars on the roads has doubled since 1990.
items.model_answer: The number of cars on the roads has doubled since 1990.
items.explanation: 'Cars' is a plural countable noun, so use 'the number of'. 'The amount of' is only for uncountable nouns (the amount of traffic, the amount of fuel).

items.prompt: Young people today have much more opportunities to travel than their parents did.
accepted_answers: Young people today have many more opportunities to travel than their parents did.
Young people today have far more opportunities to travel than their parents did.
items.model_answer: Young people today have many more opportunities to travel than their parents did.
items.explanation: Before a plural countable noun, the comparative quantifier is 'many more' (many more opportunities); 'much more' is for uncountable nouns (much more freedom). 'Far more' works with both.

items.prompt: Rural schools often lack basic equipments such as computers and science kits.
accepted_answers: Rural schools often lack basic equipment such as computers and science kits.
items.model_answer: Rural schools often lack basic equipment such as computers and science kits.
items.explanation: 'Equipment' is uncountable and has no plural form. To count individual items, use 'pieces of equipment' or name the items.

items.prompt: Pollution is one of the most serious problem facing modern cities.
accepted_answers: Pollution is one of the most serious problems facing modern cities.
items.model_answer: Pollution is one of the most serious problems facing modern cities.
items.explanation: 'One of the + superlative' is always followed by a plural noun, because it means one item from a larger group (one of the most serious problems).
